vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: chain-of-consciousness
Version: 0.1.0

The skill provides a cryptographic provenance system for AI agents to maintain tamper-evident audit trails of their actions. It involves local file operations and optional network calls to RFC 3161 timestamp authorities (e.g., freetsa.org) for anchoring, which is consistent with its stated purpose. No evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or harmful prompt injection was found in SKILL.md or README.md.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent with its stated purpose (local cryptographic provenance using a Python package); the main residual risk is that it instructs you to install and run an external PyPI package and optionally contact timestamping services, which cannot be audited from the SKILL.md alone.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the instructions: the skill directs the agent to use the 'chain-of-consciousness' Python package and CLI to create and verify hash-linked audit chains. Required binaries (python3, pip) and file access (local chain files) are appropriate for this purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are narrowly scoped to creating, adding, verifying, exporting, and optionally anchoring chains. They reference only chain files the user specifies. One area to note: optional anchoring submits chain hashes to third-party timestamp services (e.g., freetsa.org / RFC 3161), which involves outbound network calls and sharing a chain hash with external services — expected for anchoring but worth awareness.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No bundled code in the skill; it tells users to 'pip install chain-of-consciousness' from PyPI. Using pip for a Python package is normal, but installation pulls code from an external registry that cannot be audited from the skill alone — moderate supply-chain risk. There are no obscure download URLs or archive extracts in the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no environment variables, no credential needs, and no special config paths. That is proportional to the stated functionality (local file storage and optional network anchoring).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request elevated or persistent system-wide privileges. It runs as an invocable skill and may execute the coc CLI via subprocess — expected for a CLI-based workflow.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent: it uses a Python package/CLI to manage local provenance chains and optionally anchors hashes to timestamping services. Before installing: (1) review the chain-of-consciousness PyPI package page and its source repository (code, recent releases, maintainers), (2) consider installing into a virtualenv or isolated environment, (3) be aware that anchoring will send the chain hash to external timestamp services (this is intentional but leaks the hash), and (4) if you must verify the 'no telemetry' claim, inspect the package source for network/telemetry code before trusting it with sensitive data. If you want higher assurance, ask the publisher for the package source URL or include a vetted vendor/repository link in the skill metadata.
